solves: Shows the path to the current page and leads back to each level above, so the person can go up a level in a hierarchy.
use_when: On a page that sits inside a hierarchy, when the person needs to go up a level.
Choose the trail by the real path of the page: 2, 3 or 4 levels drawn, or collapsed when the path does not fit the width.
collapsed on a narrow screen: the trail keeps one line, with the first level and the last two in view.
Icons when the trail needs them, on every level; without icons, on none.
At the top of the page content, above the title.
do_not_use_when: As the navigation menu of the product: the trail shows where the page is, not where the person can go; use the navigation menu.
As tabs that switch the content of one page: use tabs.
As a back button: the trail leads to the levels of the path, and does not show the history of visited pages.
For a path with a single level: the trail has at least the first level and the current page.
As a loading state: while the page loads, a line of nph-skeleton takes the place of the trail.

levels.constraint: Property only. The path, in order, from the first level to the current page, as a list of { label, href, icon }. label is required, already localized, on one line. href is required on every level above the current page and forbidden on the last one, which is the current page. href takes http, https, mailto, tel or a relative address; any other protocol, javascript among them, in any spelling the browser reads as such, is refused. icon is optional, a core name of nph-icon, all the levels or none. The first level reads Home. A list that is not a list, has fewer than 2 levels, or breaks a rule above draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause.

collapsed.constraint: It is the Figma value `recolhido` of the property `niveis`. Off, the trail draws all its levels, 2, 3 or 4, the counts of the accepted Figma set; more than 4 levels draws nothing and emits console.error in development. On, it draws the first level, the ellipsis button and the last two levels, and the levels in between sit in the menu the button opens; it needs 4 levels or more, and fewer draws nothing and emits console.error in development. The consumer chooses it, since the width is the page to know. Reflects so the consumer can style and check the state.

label.constraint: The accessible name of the navigation landmark, already localized. It wins over the aria-label of the host. A trail with neither draws and warns once in development.

ellipsis-label.constraint: The accessible name of the ellipsis button, already localized, such as Show hidden levels. Required on the collapsed trail, because the icon has no text; without it the collapsed trail draws nothing and emits console.error in development. Not read when the trail is not collapsed.

aria-label.constraint: The accessible name of the landmark when label is not given; label wins over it. It is read by a property whose attribute is aria-label, since a property called ariaLabel is the native ARIA reflection of the element. A trail with neither draws and warns once in development.

trail.choose_when: 2, 3 or 4 levels drawn when the path fits the width, the Figma values 2, 3 and 4 of `niveis`; collapsed (`recolhido`) when the path has 4 levels or more and does not fit, or on a narrow screen.

icons.choose_when: Without icons (sem) when the text is enough; with icons (com) when each level has a figure that helps to recognize it. Every level has an icon, or none does.
do_not_combine_with: an icon on only some of the levels
an icon that does not belong to the core of nph-icon

link-rest.changes_for_user: The level shows in the muted color, in regular weight, with no underline.

link-hover.changes_for_user: The text and the icon take the stronger color and the text is underlined, so color is not the only signal.

link-focus.changes_for_user: For keyboard users, the text and the icon take the stronger color and a border and a halo outside the link mark the focus.

current.changes_for_user: The last level shows in the strongest color and in medium weight, with the solid icon when there are icons. It is text, not a link: it has no hover and takes no focus.

ellipsis-rest.changes_for_user: The ellipsis icon shows in the muted color, with no background.

ellipsis-hover.changes_for_user: The icon takes the stronger color and the button takes a background.

ellipsis-focus.changes_for_user: For keyboard users, a border and a halo outside the button mark the focus; the icon keeps the color of rest.

ellipsis-open.changes_for_user: While the menu of hidden levels is open, the button keeps the look of hover, even with the pointer away.

business_rules: The last level of levels is the current page: it is text, it carries aria-current page, and it has no href. Every level above it is a link and has an href.
The first level reads Home. With icons, the house goes next to the text, never alone: the icon alone does not say where the link leads.
The collapsed trail draws the first level, the ellipsis and the last two levels. The levels in between sit in the menu of the ellipsis, in path order, as text only, with no header and no group label.
With icons, every level has its own: light on a link and solid on the current page, in the same color as its label. The two never mix in one trail.
The consumer chooses collapsed. The piece does not collapse by itself when the width runs short.
The trail is on one line: it never wraps and never shrinks.

Activating a hidden level in the menu leads where its visible link would: the piece clicks a hidden anchor of its own shadow root with the same href, so the native click bubbles, is composed and cancelable. The piece fires no event of its own.

The hidden levels menu hugs its widest option between the floor and the ceiling of breadcrumb/menu-min-width and breadcrumb/menu-max-width, with the text cut by an ellipsis past the ceiling. It holds only in the breadcrumb; nph-dropdown-menu keeps its own fixed width.
Every text comes from the consumer, already localized: the piece writes no word of its own.
There is no loading state. While the page loads, a line of nph-skeleton takes the place of the trail.
domain_errors: A levels that is not a list, with fewer than 2 levels, or with more than 4 levels on a trail that is not collapsed: the trail draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause.
A collapsed trail with fewer than 4 levels, or without ellipsis-label: the trail draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

A level without label; a level above the current page without href; the current page with an href; an icon outside the core of nph-icon or on only some of the levels: the trail draws nothing and emits console.error in development.
A trail with no accessible name draws and warns once in development, because the name may arrive after the first render.

tokens.label: breadcrumb/font-family, breadcrumb/font-size, breadcrumb/line-height, breadcrumb/letter-spacing
tokens.focus: focus/border, border/width, focus/border-radius-control, focus/halo, focus/ring-width, focus/radius-control-with-border

ai_hints: Use nph-breadcrumb at the top of a page that sits inside a hierarchy, above the title; for the navigation of the product use the navigation menu, for tabs use tabs.
Give levels from the first level to the current page: every level above has label and href, and the last one has only label.
Write the first level as Home, and keep the labels short and equal to the title of the target page.
Choose collapsed when the trail does not fit the width, and then give ellipsis-label; the piece does not collapse by itself.
Give the trail a label, or an aria-label, because it is the accessible name of the navigation landmark.
Put an icon on every level or on none, and never on the first level alone.
While the page loads, show a line of nph-skeleton in place of the trail.

accessibility.semantics: A nav, named, holding an ordered list. Each level is a list item: a link above the current page, and the current page as text with aria-current page. The separators and the level icons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology: the name of a level is its label. The ellipsis is a native button of the shadow root, which the menu beside it finds by for and on which it writes aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.
accessibility.accessible_name: The landmark: label, else the aria-label of the host. A level: its label. The ellipsis: ellipsis-label, because its icon has no text.
keyboard: Tab moves through the links in path order, and through the ellipsis between the first level and the last two. The current page and the separators take no Tab.
On the ellipsis, Enter, Space and the down arrow open the menu of hidden levels.
In the menu, the arrows move, Enter and Space activate the level, and Esc closes the menu and gives the focus back to the ellipsis.
accessibility.focus: Keyboard only, on the link and on the ellipsis: a border of border/width in focus/border and a halo in focus/halo outside the box, without changing its size. The border carries the focus; the halo is reinforcement. The current page takes no focus.
accessibility.contrast: The links, the separator, the link icons and the ellipsis at rest, in the muted color, and the current page, in the strongest color, pass the required WCAG level over the background in both themes. The current page has the highest contrast of the trail, never lower than the links.
accessibility.color_alternative: The current page is told apart without color: it is not a link, it has medium weight and, with icons, the solid icon. The hover of a link adds the underline to the change of color.

invalid_combinations: collapsed with fewer than 4 levels — there is no level to hide.
More than 4 levels without collapsed — the contract draws 2, 3 or 4 levels.
A collapsed trail without ellipsis-label — the ellipsis has an icon and no text.
An href on the current page, or a level above it without href — the current page is text, and every level above is a link.
An icon on only some of the levels — with icons every level has one, without icons none does.
A trail with fewer than 2 levels — it has at least the first level and the current page.

parents: the top of the page content, above the title

anti_patterns: Using the trail as the navigation menu, as tabs or as a back button.
Making the current page a link.
Letting the trail wrap or overflow the width instead of collapsing it.
Putting an icon on only some of the levels.
Leaving the house alone on the first level, with no Home text.
Leaving the trail without a label or an aria-label.
